scope: reaction-level corrections proposed for the CarveMe/BiGG universe, applied to every model that contains the reaction; each patch is justified on biochemical grounds independent of the fitness data and then verified by the carbon-source fitness benchmark across organisms (fix-at-source loop, roadmap WS1)

patches.name: carbamate kinase
patches.bigg_reaction: atp_c + co2_c + nh4_c <=> adp_c + cbp_c + 2 h_c
patches.effect: catabolic direction only (carbamoyl phosphate + ADP -> ATP + CO2 + NH4)
patches.rationale: Carbamate kinase (EC 2.7.2.2) functions in the arginine deiminase and allantoin degradation pathways, where it phosphorylates ADP at the expense of carbamoyl phosphate; the synthetic direction is not a physiological route to carbamoyl phosphate in bacteria that possess glutamine-dependent carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase (carAB), and with the reaction reversible every such model predicts carAB dispensable on minimal medium, contradicting the classic arginine/pyrimidine auxotrophy of carAB mutants.
patches.flagged_by: benchmark: carbamoyl-phosphate synthase genes important in nearly every carbon-source condition but predicted dispensable in P. putida, S. meliloti and E. coli (iML1515); pFBA after carAB knockout routes all carbamoyl-phosphate synthesis through CBMKr
patches.caveat: Some archaea and a few bacteria use carbamate-kinase-like enzymes for carbamoyl-phosphate synthesis; the patch should not be applied to models without carAB.

patches.name: carbamoyl-phosphate synthase (glutamine-hydrolysing)
patches.effect: the gene rule keeps only the subunit conjunctions: 'A or B or C or (A and B)' becomes '(A and B)'; standalone genes are dropped because no single polypeptide catalyses the glutamine-dependent reaction (in S. oneidensis the standalone gene was the aspartate carbamoyltransferase pyrB, a mis-assignment)
patches.rationale: Glutamine-dependent carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase is an obligate heterodimer of the small glutaminase subunit (carA) and the large synthetase subunit (carB); mutants in either subunit are arginine/pyrimidine auxotrophs in E. coli, P. aeruginosa and B. subtilis. CarveMe merges gene rules from several source models and produces 'carA or carB or (carA and carB)', under which no single-subunit knockout removes the reaction.
patches.flagged_by: benchmark: carA and carB important in every carbon-source condition but predicted dispensable in S. meliloti and S. oneidensis after the CBMKr patch; the rule shape '(A and B) or A or B' occurs in 7-30 reactions per draft model
patches.caveat: Applies to the glutamine-dependent enzyme (carAB); ammonia-dependent single-chain CPS (as in some archaea or the mammalian CPS1) is a different enzyme.

patches.name: urate oxidase
patches.bigg_reaction: 2 h2o_c + o2_c + urate_c --> alltn_c + co2_c + h2o2_c
patches.rationale: iML1515 carries urate oxidase without a gene. E. coli K-12 has no uricase and cannot degrade urate; its allantoin utilisation genes (allABCD, ybbY/allP) act on exogenous allantoin. With URIC open the model routes de novo purines through urate, allantoin and oxalurate to oxamate carbamoyltransferase and so makes carbamoyl-phosphate synthetase (carAB) dispensable on every carbon source, contradicting the auxotrophy of carAB mutants and their strong fitness defects.
patches.flagged_by: benchmark: carA (b0032) and carB (b0033) important in 30 of 32 conditions but never predicted essential by iML1515; pFBA after carA knockout with carbamate kinase restricted routes all carbamoyl phosphate through URIC -> ... -> OXAMTC
patches.caveat: scoped to E. coli; organisms with a genuine uricase keep the reaction

patches.name: phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (ATP)
patches.effect: reversible (carboxylating direction PEP + CO2 + ADP -> OAA + ATP allowed)
patches.rationale: The CarveMe universe carries PEP carboxykinase only in the gluconeogenic direction inherited from E. coli. Bacteroides species run PckA carboxylating as the entry to the succinate-propionate pathway (PEP -> oxaloacetate -> malate -> fumarate -> succinate -> propionate), their principal anaplerotic and fermentative route; B. thetaiotaomicron has no PEP carboxylase, and its draft therefore had to route all oxaloacetate formation through pyruvate carboxylase, whose subunits have no fitness phenotype.
patches.flagged_by: benchmark: the v0.3 pyruvate-carboxylase subunit rule (R2) made PC essential in every B. thetaiotaomicron condition although the PC subunit genes have no phenotype; a false isozyme in the shipped rule had masked the missing anaplerotic route
patches.caveat: scoped to B. thetaiotaomicron (and applicable to other Bacteroidetes with a succinate-propionate pathway); in E. coli and most aerobes PckA is gluconeogenic and the reaction should stay irreversible
